raw_response:
Answer: A
Reason: The chest X-rays show peripheral, patchy opacities that are more prominent in the lower lung zones, a pattern classically associated with eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis (EGPA) in patients with asthma and nasal polyposis. This distribution helps distinguish it from other conditions like sarcoidosis (central/perilymphatic) or tuberculosis (apical).
